newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Senate committees discuss telecom bill.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Senate committees discuss telecom bill.

text.p: Three committees in Brazil's Senate met in a joint session Tuesday to discuss and possibly vote on a bill that paves the way for privatization of the country's huge telecommunications industry, officials said.

The bill, which has already been approved in the Chamber of Deputies, regulates a constitutional amendment approved in 1995 which opens up Brazil's state telecommunications monopoly to private competitition.

The General Telecommunications Law would set down rules for the privatization of the federal Telebras system, create a new regulator and establish the terms for private companies operating in the sector.

The bill does not set any limits on foreign capital in Brazilian telecommunications operators but would give the president of the republic powers to restrict non-Brazilian investors on a case-by-case basis.
If approved by the committees, the legislation advances to the floor of the Senate where it may be voted later this week.
